terms.title: The work
terms.body: I review the MyAlly code, database rules and build spec and deliver what is listed in Exhibit A. That's all Step 1 includes. Steps 2 and 3 stay at {{fee_step1}} each if you choose to go on. They, the full build, a pilot and any launch each need their own written yes.

terms.title: Fee
terms.body: Step 1 is a fixed {{fee_step1}} for everything in Exhibit A, including the rough numbers and the walkthrough call. If it takes me longer than I planned, that's on me. I would only charge more for something outside Exhibit A, and only after your written yes, at {{rate_ff}} an hour. I'll invoice {{client.legal_name}} on signing, and payment is due on signing.

terms.title: Timing
terms.body: I'll deliver within {{work_days|word}} working days after I have GitHub and Lovable access, or after signing if that comes later. Delays on your side move the date by the same amount.

terms.title: Office hours
terms.body: {{oh_free_hours}} hours a month at no charge, in {{oh_slot_minutes}}-minute slots, to use however you like. Extra hours are {{rate_standard}} an hour, or {{rate_committed}} an hour when booked for {{commit_weeks}} weeks or more.

terms.title: What you own
terms.body: Once paid, I assign to you all rights in the report and anything else I deliver in Step 1. I keep my pre-existing tools, templates and methods, including ARCS (NDA sections 9.2 and 9.3). Where any of them are built into what I deliver, {{client.legal_name}}, and any company that takes over the MyAlly project, gets a permanent, royalty-free license to use, change and pass them on as part of the MyAlly platform, including to another developer working on it for you.

terms.title: Estimates
terms.body: Any ranges or estimates are my good-faith planning numbers for work I would do. They aren't a quote, a fixed price or a promise, and nobody else can rely on them as one. You're welcome to use them in your business plan and with investors, funders and advisors. If you share them, please share them as my estimates, with the assumptions attached.

terms.title: My opinion, not legal or compliance advice
terms.body: I'll do the work carefully and professionally. My findings are my professional opinion, for you to use as you see fit, and the decisions remain yours. The data check is a careful read of the code and database rules. It isn't a full security test, and it isn't a legal or compliance review under student-records law (FERPA), children's online privacy law (COPPA), health-privacy law (HIPAA) or state privacy law. A full test comes later, and for legal questions you'll want a specialist.

terms.title: Fixes, and code as is
terms.body: If something I deliver doesn't match Exhibit A, tell me within {{fix_window_days}} days and I'll fix it. Any code, configuration or setup is provided as is, without other warranties. Running, maintaining, hosting, securing and backing up the platform remains your responsibility, unless a later written agreement says otherwise.

terms.title: Your data
terms.body: Please don't send me real family or child information; I review the rules, not the records. For the access you give me: I'll use only what you give me, I won't copy family records, I'll keep your data out of AI tools except as NDA section 4 allows, I'll tell you within {{breach_notice_hours}} hours if I suspect any exposure, and I'll give back all access when Step 1 ends unless a later step is signed.

terms.title: Limit of liability
terms.body: My total liability under this agreement is capped at {{liability_cap}}, and neither of us is liable for indirect or lost-profit damages. The cap doesn't apply to breaches of the NDA, or to gross negligence or willful misconduct.

terms.title: Covering each other
terms.body: Each of us covers the other for claims from third parties caused by our own negligence or breach of this agreement or the NDA. I also cover you if anything I deliver infringes someone else's rights. You cover me for claims about your platform, users and data, except where I caused the problem.

terms.title: Disputes
terms.body: We talk first, in good faith, for {{talk_first_days}} days. After that, either of us can go to {{dispute_forum}}, including small claims. Connecticut law applies.

terms.title: The NDA stays
terms.body: The Mutual NDA (executed {{nda_executed|nda}}) continues to apply, and this agreement counts as the services agreement in its section 8.1. If {{nda_restart_days}} days pass after Step 1 is delivered with no later step signed, NDA section 8.1(c) applies again. If the two conflict on confidentiality, the NDA controls.

terms.title: Ending early
terms.body: I'm an independent contractor, not an employee. Either of us can end this agreement in writing. If either of us ends it early, I refund the part of the fee for work not yet done. Sections 5, 6, 10, 11, 12 and 13 survive if this agreement ends.

terms.title: The basics
terms.body: This agreement and the NDA are the whole agreement between us for Step 1. Changes must be in writing. E-signatures are fine. Notices go by email to the addresses below.

altitudes.operational: Three steps, each with its own written yes. Step 1 runs about {{duration_days|weeks}} from access.
altitudes.tactical: Chelsea's four asks, each answered by a named part of this record: deliverables, estimates, the delivery date and the agreement.
altitudes.surgical: Every value, where it came from, and when it last changed.

cold_read.why_now: The holding reply promised a follow-up. They want results before year end, and the NDA's return-or-destroy clause (8.1(c)) fires {{nda_return_by|long}} unless a services agreement is signed first.
cold_read.before: Agreement signed and GitHub and Lovable access by {{access_by|long}}.
cold_read.during: Step 1 runs about {{duration_days|weeks}}, {{hours_step1}} hours of my time, from {{access_by}} to {{deliver_by}}.
cold_read.after: A {{walkthrough_minutes}}-minute walkthrough by {{deliver_by|long}}, then their written yes or no on Step 2.

counsel_notes: Option B (mutual indemnity, the NDA's Connecticut courts) already meets counsel's usual pushback points. Likely questions: the liability cap amount (term 10), the 30-day fix window (term 8) and the scope of the data check (term 7). Hold firm on terms 6, 7 and 10.
